title: Comparison: UPSC vs State Public Service Commission

blocks.content: Although the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor, they can be removed only by the President and not by the Governor.

items: Frequent Exam Trap: Governors can APPOINT SPSC members, but ONLY the President can REMOVE them after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
Age Limit Difference: UPSC age criteria is 6/65 years, whereas SPSC age criteria is 6/62 years.
Annual Reports Destination: UPSC reports to the President (placed before Parliament); SPSC reports to the Governor (placed before State Legislature).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Both UPSC and SPSC are independent constitutional bodies established under Article 315 in Part XIV of the Constitution of India.
Members of UPSC are appointed by the President, whereas SPSC members are appointed by the Governor of the respective State.
SPSC members can be removed ONLY by the President of India, not by the Governor, on the same grounds and procedure as UPSC members.
The tenure for members of both commissions is 6 years, but the maximum age limit is 65 years for UPSC and 62 years for SPSC.
UPSC presents its annual report to the President, while SPSC presents its annual report to the Governor of the State.
